CVE-2026-46718 affects calcite-core 1.37.0 (unsafe reflection vulnerability). The fix is available in calcite-core 1.42.0. However, Druid's pom.xml uses a Maven property ${calcite.version} for version management, and the mvn/patch@v1 tool cannot override property-based versions in dependencyManagement. A direct upgrade requires either upstream Druid to bump the property or a more invasive patch mechanism. Investigation is ongoing for a safe upgrade path that does not break Druid's SQL query planning.

CVE-2026-56741 is the CVE identifier for the JLine3 Telnet server (remote-telnet module) CPU-exhaustion DoS tracked as GHSA-2r2c-cx56-8933: TelnetIO.handleNAWS() accepts attacker-supplied NAWS terminal dimensions with only a lower bound and drives redisplay() up to 65534 iterations per event. Druid does not instantiate or expose a JLine Telnet server; jline is bundled as a transitive dependency (via the org.jline:jline uber-jar) for CLI line-reading only. The telnet server code is present in the uber-jar but is never loaded or executed in Druid's runtime. The fix exists only in jline 4.x (all 3.x versions are affected) and upgrading is a major version change incompatible with the current dependency tree.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

statements.status_notes: Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
